candidates.title: Data Contracts
candidates.author: Simon Harrer and Arif Wider (published by Martin Fowler)
candidates.organization: martinfowler.com / Entropy Data / Thoughtworks / HTW Berlin
candidates.pub_date: 2026-11-18 (recent-changes: Wed 18 Nov 2026 09:02 EST = 14:02 UTC; article byline 18 November 2026)
candidates.what_changed: Long-form guide to data contracts using the Open Data Contract Standard (ODCS); highlights ODCS 3.2 (2026) 'AI context' block written specifically for agents, plus the Data Contract CLI CI/CD workflow.
candidates.mechanism: YAML contract (kind: DataContract) per dataset covering schema, quality rules, ownership/support, terms of use/SLAs, server locations, IAM roles, AI context, price. AI context = 'instructions' (acts like a system prompt for the dataset, e.g. premiums stored in cents), 'constraints' (what an agent must not do, e.g. no decisions about individual customers), and 'verifiedStatements' (business question paired with provider-checked SQL an agent can reuse). Contracts live in git next to pipeline code (naming: customers_pii_snowflake_v1.odcs.yaml), SemVer with major version tied to dataset; CI stages: `datacontract lint`, `datacontract breaking` (vs previous version), `datacontract ci` (test data per environment), then `datacontract publish` to marketplace; nightly cron `datacontract test --server prod`.
candidates.evidence_quality: Practitioner/vendor-authored design guide (lead author is CEO of Entropy Data and on ODCS steering committee); worked YAML examples; no quantitative evaluation of agent accuracy gains. Claims '1 million downloads per month' for Data Contract CLI and Thoughtworks Radar 'Trial' (Nov 2025) are author-stated.
candidates.independent_confirmation: Partial: Thoughtworks Radar rating cited by authors (not re-checked); ODCS 3.2 AI context not independently verified here (UNVERIFIED beyond article).
candidates.relevance: HIGH. Concrete, try-this-week pattern for 'chat with your data' and agent-built pipelines: add an AI context block (instructions/constraints/verified SQL) to dataset contracts and gate merges with datacontract lint/breaking/ci. Also describes spec-driven pipeline generation: contract + company skills plugin fed to a coding agent, with tests against the contract as feedback loop; and short-lived (minutes) access agreements for agents (OAAS RFC).
candidates.overlap_with_prior: Adjacent to Ed2 harness-enforced checks / runtime contracts and skills topics, but materially new: data-layer contracts for agents rather than agent-harness checks.
candidates.summary: Harrer and Wider argue data contracts apply API-design practice to datasets and become essential when consumers are agents: a human who distrusts data hesitates or asks the owner, while an agent 'treats every value as truth' and produces confidently wrong results. ODCS (Bitol project, Linux Foundation) is now the de facto standard after ODCS 3.1 support in Data Contract CLI retired the older Data Contract Specification; ODCS 3.2 (2026) added an AI context section. Example contract fields: schema/quality, owner and support channels, terms of use and SLAs, server locations (test/staging/prod as separate server entries), roles mapping to platform IAM roles (e.g. Snowflake), AI context, price (e.g. 10 USD per TB scanned), custom properties. Practices: contract-first vs data-first; keep contracts in the pipeline repo; SemVer with breaking changes shipped as a new major version alongside a new dataset and phased in/out (draft->active->deprecated->retired); for event streams use forward/full compatibility (warning: schema-registry backward-compat default permits field deletion, which breaks consumers); exclude SELECT * so adding columns is non-breaking. CI: datacontract lint / breaking / ci / publish, plus nightly datacontract test --server prod. Benefits section: 'Generate your data pipeline' (coding agent + contract + skills plugin, data tested against contract as feedback loop; example on dataproduct.com) and 'Chat with your data' where the hard part is correct SQL, discovered via a marketplace searchable through MCP. Access agreements: bilateral, provider-approved, time-bound (for agents possibly a few minutes); Open Access Agreement Standard is an RFC. Costs acknowledged: not worth writing for every dataset.

candidates.title: GPT-6.2 Astra, the #2 Frontier Model is better and 20%-600% cheaper, but has mixed reviews; 6.2 Sol likely main workhorse
candidates.author: swyx
candidates.what_changed: Daily news roundup of OpenAI GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol launch plus agent-harness and inference cost findings.
candidates.mechanism: Aggregated claims: API prices Astra $8 in / $0.40 cached / $40 out per M tokens; Sol $2/$0.10/$10; both 1M context, 128K output. Harness/cost items: Baseten measured up to 4.4x spread in cost per passing task across 22 harnesses x 5 open models; SemiAnalysis: 1.8% of uncached requests = ~15% of spend in its sample; Hugging Face Pi adapter lifted Qwen3.8-27B 15->32 solves on 51 hardest SWE-bench Pro tasks with 55% fewer tool calls (corrected next day to 20->33); Google SIM-evolved harness tuned on Opus scored 68.41 on Gemini vs 73.89 for the starting harness; HF 1,000-agent run: only 40-60 agents calling the model at once, ~130 tokens read per token written; vLLM sliding-window draft up to 30% higher acceptance length for Kimi K3.1 Pro.
candidates.evidence_quality: Secondary aggregation of vendor and third-party posts (Artificial Analysis, Vals, Mercor, Baseten, SemiAnalysis, HF); numbers are as reported by those sources, not reproduced. The Pi adapter figure was corrected the next day.
candidates.independent_confirmation: Mixed: Artificial Analysis/Vals/Mercor independent of OpenAI for benchmark numbers; harness-cost claims single-source (UNVERIFIED).
candidates.relevance: MEDIUM-HIGH. Actionable for model routing/pricing (Sol at ~15% of cost per task of prior Astra per Artificial Analysis) and for measuring harness cost and cache-miss tail spend.
candidates.overlap_with_prior: High overlap: Ed2 used simonwillison.net/2026/Nov/17/gpt62-astra-and-sol/ and Epoch real-work eval; cache-miss and cost-per-task items overlap prefix caching and cost per solved task topics. New detail: Baseten 4.4x harness spread, SemiAnalysis 1.8%->15% cache-miss tail, harness-specialization result.
candidates.summary: Artificial Analysis: new Astra scores 62 on Intelligence Index vs Fable 5.2 at 65; Sol ties September's Astra at ~15% of the cost per task. OpenAI-reported: Agents' Last Exam 1.1 Astra xhigh +5.2 pts over GPT-6 Astra max at <1/3 cost per task; GDPval v2 22% fewer output tokens. Mercor OpenWorldEngineer: Astra 67.2%, Fable 5.2 54.6%, GPT-6 Astra 44.2%. Perplexity WANDR: Astra 0.783 at ~$12.54/task, Sol 0.746 at ~$2.65. OpenAI rated Astra High for AI Self-Improvement in its preparedness framework (first for an externally released model). Strongly negative influencer reviews (Matt Shumer 'essentially unusable'; Schirano blamed harness). Microsoft Ignite: MAI Code 2 / Code 2 Flash in Copilot; Copilot Fusion multi-model harness 71.2% Terminal-Bench 4.1 at 88% lower cost than Fable 5.2 (vendor-reported). Harness section: Baseten 4.4x cost-per-passing-task spread across 22 harnesses; SIM harness specialization (68.41 vs 73.89 on Gemini); Perplexity mixed-model teams beat 4x lead model; Replit diminishing returns 16->32 agents; HF 1,000-agent run coordination-bound (40-60 concurrently calling model, ~130:1 read:write tokens); SemiAnalysis 1.8% of uncached requests ~15% of spend. Also Marin 57 intermediate checkpoints, K2 Horizon decoding adapter 2.2x, Zyphra 9-60x at 10M tokens, vLLM speculative decoding gains.

candidates.title: Gemini 4 Neon: GDM's Opus/Sol Contender
candidates.author: swyx
candidates.what_changed: Roundup of Google's Gemini 4 Neon launch, follow-up GPT-6.2 results, OpenAI Responses API background-job discounts, and harness/token-efficiency research.
candidates.mechanism: Neon pricing $3 in / $0.15 cached / $15 out per M tokens, 1M context, four effort levels. OpenAI public beta: GPT-6.2 Responses API jobs that can wait, with 2-hour and 8-hour first-response targets at 30% and 40% per-token discounts. DAIR summary: gated approach editing one harness module at a time scored 40.0% SWE-bench Lite at 46.7K tokens/task vs full rewrite 42.5% at 451.6K tokens (40-issue held-out). HF Pi adapter corrected to 20->33 solves (39.2%->64.7%) after a tunnel outage hit nine base runs; OpenCode adapter moved Qwen3.8-27B 35.3%->51.0% thinking off. vLLM 0.34.0: extensible KV cache on by default, Model Runner V2 sole GPU runner, up to 1.95x faster NVFP4 decode on GB200.
candidates.evidence_quality: Secondary aggregation; benchmark numbers from Artificial Analysis, Vals, Agent Arena, Cursor; hands-on logs from individual testers (13 sessions). Includes a published correction of prior-day figures (good practice).
candidates.independent_confirmation: Partial: Neon pricing also reported by Simon Willison (https://simonwillison.net/2026/Nov/18/llm-gemini/) matching $3/$15. Background-discount and DAIR figures single-source (UNVERIFIED).
candidates.relevance: HIGH for cost-conscious teams: background/flex Responses API jobs at 30-40% off are a direct configuration change for batch agent work; one-module-at-a-time harness editing as a 10x token saver; Neon at high effort matching Carbon's Intelligence Index (60) at $3.74/task.
candidates.overlap_with_prior: Partial overlap with cost per solved task topic; Neon itself is new since Ed2.
candidates.summary: Gemini 4 Neon is Google's fourth Gemini 4 model in ~7 weeks; Argon retired; lineup now Carbon/Neon/Hydrogen. Rollout: paid Gemini API in AI Studio/Android Studio, Gemini for business, Antigravity; day-one in Cursor, GitHub Copilot (app, CLI, VS Code), LangChain Managed Deep Agents. Independent results: Artificial Analysis Neon high = Carbon's 60 at $3.74/task; GDP.pdf 33.4% high vs 28.0% xhigh (more effort scored lower); Agent Arena #2 (1,336, ~4,200 sessions, $2.82 median task cost); Vals Index 70.9%, ~0.4 pt behind Fable 5.2 at < half the cost; Code Migration averaged 160 turns vs Carbon 234 / Hydrogen 574 but scored below both; CursorBench 4.1 63.7% vs Hydrogen 57.3%. Hands-on: 13 Antigravity sessions, 762 tool calls, 93% input-cache hit rate, zero shell commands when told to avoid terminal, but 57 capacity errors and 4 stalled runs. Theo's split: Neon for copy, Fable to implement, Astra to playtest; Jeremy Howard reverted Solveit's Astra/Sol to pre-6.2. GPT-6.2 follow-ups: MathArena top two; Astra 42/53 ArXivLean; Artificial Analysis found Astra responses shorter and less likely to admit uncertainty after final changes. Responses API background jobs: 30%/40% discounts for 2h/8h targets. Infra: vLLM 0.34.0; Epoch: inference capacity for agent workloads grew 4.6x Q2 2025->Q2 2026 vs 2.6x peak 8-bit compute; MAC Bench: most 8-agent gains from parallel exploration, only Opus 5.5 gained from coordination. Industry: Anthropic IPO priced $83; Palo Alto Networks to buy Applied Compute ($4.5B).

candidates.title: Anthropic successfully completes largest IPO in history, valued at $1.5T
candidates.author: swyx
candidates.what_changed: Roundup dominated by Anthropic's Nasdaq IPO, with a practitioner tail on open adapters, Responses API usage guidance, self-improving harnesses and eval releases.
candidates.mechanism: Practitioner items: HF harness-hub LoRA adapters for Qwen3.8-27B (~300MB, Apache 2.0, trained with TRL AsyncGRPOTrainer + OpenEnv): OpenCode adapter SWE-bench Pro hard 35.3->51.0, Terminal-Bench 2.1 46.4->52.4, median turns 48->13; Hermes adapter thinking-off 29.4->43.1 and TB2.1 44.7->58.8, matching base xhigh with 3.5-4.4x fewer tokens. OpenAI Devs: in the Responses API append history rather than editing it to preserve reasoning items. OpenClaw setting to keep reasoning content reportedly raised score 44%. Google GUARD self-improving harness 80.8% on 43 SDK tasks with 54.5% fewer tokens vs Meta-Harness. Perplexity self-writing skills 8-week RCT: tool failures -11%, dissatisfied threads -7.6%. AutoRLBench: agents detect unhealthy RL runs 82.6% but root-cause only 28.2%. Reward-hack defenses broken by comma-vs-space change. Stripe open-sourced integration evals. OpenAI Codex Performance Factory: 1,700+ regression investigations, 600+ root causes in ~3 months. GPT-Live-1.1 standby $0.02/min vs $0.05.
candidates.evidence_quality: Secondary aggregation of tweets; most practitioner figures single-source and self-reported; headline and title valuations inconsistent within the issue ($1.5T title vs ~$2T fully diluted at open).
candidates.independent_confirmation: UNVERIFIED for most practitioner items; IPO pricing ($83) also stated in prior Latent Space issue.
candidates.relevance: MEDIUM. Mostly finance news; useful nuggets: Responses API append-don't-edit rule (configuration fix), small LoRA harness adapters that cut turns/tokens for local open models, Stripe integration evals.
candidates.overlap_with_prior: Overlaps skills/goal engineering (self-writing skills) and private evals; harness adapters are new.
candidates.summary: ANT priced at $83, opened $111.50 (+34.3%), closed $97.17; $81.3B raise the largest IPO ever (beating SpaceX $75B); expected net proceeds $104.8B incl. private placement; AMD investing $2.5B. Dario Amodei remarks commit to pacing training/deployment until confident systems are safe and under human control; Class F shares hold 50.1% voting power. S-1 commentary: ~$140B raised, ~$132B on balance sheet. Gemini 4 family pricing restated (Carbon $4/$20, Neon $3/$15, Hydrogen $1.50/$7.50; Neon/Hydrogen add xhigh); Cognition FrontierCode 2.0 Neon 46.2% within 1 pt of Opus 5.5 at ~1/3 cost ($4.38/task); Vals RSI Index full run $475 Neon vs $1,536 Fable 5.2 vs $1,647 Opus 5.5 (criticized as 4 tasks, single runs). Google also opened Genie 4 in the Gemini API (Live Interactions API) and Tool Retrieval. Microsoft Ignite: MAI Code 2 claims 96% of Opus 5.5 at 5% cost. Practitioner tail as listed in mechanism (HF adapters, Responses API append rule, GUARD, Perplexity skills RCT, AutoRLBench, Stripe evals, Codex Performance Factory, alphaXiv agent preprint server: ~1,000 agents from 35 labs, 936 papers in 12 weeks). Security: Dragos seeded 2M canaries exposing 3 compromised providers and ZDR violations; OpenRouter disclosure of Prime Intellect compromise (UNVERIFIED).

candidates.title: Scaling Linear’s GTM to $100M ARR — Cristina Cordova, COO
candidates.author: Basil Chatha (host page); guest Cristina Cordova
candidates.what_changed: Interview: more than half of issues created in Linear now come from agents (3% a year ago), via its MCP server (May 2025), agent platform and integrations.
candidates.mechanism: Linear MCP server + agent platform + integrations (Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot) + Linear Agent; Cordova tracks two lines, agent usage vs app usage, as a commoditization signal; Linear won't let an LLM answer support tickets on its own.
candidates.evidence_quality: Company executive self-report in interview; no external data.
candidates.relevance: LOW-MEDIUM for practitioners: the 'agent usage vs app usage' metric is a usable product-instrumentation idea for teams exposing MCP servers; otherwise GTM-focused.
candidates.summary: Linear (~$100M ARR, 40,000+ paying customers, 177% NRR, $2.5B valuation tender in August) repositioned after 'Issue tracking is dead' toward a product development system built around agent orchestration. Agents created 3% of Linear's work a year ago, now >50% of issues. Cordova warns SaaS companies against becoming 'a database with an MCP server on top'; if agent usage climbs and app usage does not, you're becoming a commodity. Also: no SDRs, stopped chasing enterprise deals early, no fully autonomous LLM support answers, AI budgets accelerating purchases.

candidates.title: Release: datasette-arrows 0.1a0
candidates.author: Simon Willison
candidates.what_changed: New Datasette plugin adding Apache Arrow streaming export, built almost single-shot by Claude Fable 5.2.
candidates.mechanism: Uses Datasette 1.0a43's register_output_renderer() plugin hook, which now supports streaming export formats (as CSV/TSV already did), so millions of rows can be exported without loading into memory; Arrow IPC streaming format suggested by Fable 5.2.
candidates.evidence_quality: First-hand author report; code release on GitHub.
candidates.independent_confirmation: Release exists at https://github.com/datasette/datasette-arrows/releases/tag/0.1a0 (linked; not separately fetched).
candidates.relevance: LOW-MEDIUM. Practice note: 'never release a new plugin feature without accompanying it with a plugin that uses it' - and a coding agent can produce that reference plugin cheaply.
candidates.summary: Datasette 1.0a43 allows plugins to implement streaming export formats via register_output_renderer(). To exercise the hook, Willison had Claude Fable 5.2 propose and build an Arrow streaming exporter 'in almost a single shot'. `datasette install datasette-arrows` adds an Arrow option to the export dialog; grouping with CSV/TSV under 'All rows' lands in the next alpha.

candidates.title: A quote from Daniel Stenberg
candidates.author: Simon Willison (quoting Daniel Stenberg)
candidates.what_changed: Stenberg's counterpoint to agent-driven C-to-Rust rewrites of curl: the original kept moving faster than the clones.
candidates.mechanism: Maintenance-drift argument: agent ports freeze a snapshot while upstream continues to land fixes.
candidates.evidence_quality: Quote from the curl maintainer with his own counts; original post not fetched (host blocked by proxy: 403 'no rule or network setting allows this host').
candidates.relevance: MEDIUM as a cautionary metric for 'vibe-porting': measure upstream commit/bugfix velocity during and after an agent port, not just line counts.
candidates.summary: During the period agents converted 185,000 lines of C into 340,000 lines of Rust, the real curl project merged 300+ commits in a little over three weeks, including ~200 bugfixes and a few vulnerability fixes that none of the Rust rewrites have; another ~200 fixes followed the next month. 'Will these clones keep up?' Tagged coding-agents, vibe-porting.

candidates.title: PostgreSQL 19 Released
candidates.author: Simon Willison
candidates.what_changed: Link post on PostgreSQL 19, delayed two months mainly by the volume of AI-reported vulnerabilities; highlights WAIT FOR LSN read-your-writes on standbys.
candidates.mechanism: SELECT pg_current_wal_insert_lsn() after a write, store LSN (e.g. signed cookie), then on a standby `WAIT FOR LSN '0/0306EE20' WITH (TIMEOUT '0.1s');` before reading; mirrors MediaWiki's MySQL WAIT_FOR_EXECUTED_GTID_SET()/SOURCE_POS_WAIT() pattern.
candidates.evidence_quality: Release notes plus worked example; release-delay attribution cites Robert Haas post (linked, not fetched).
candidates.relevance: LOW for AI practitioners (database feature); AI angle is the AI-reported vulnerability load delaying a major release.
candidates.summary: PostgreSQL 19 shipped in November rather than September because of the 'ongoing AI-reported vulnerability apocalypse'. Favorite feature: read-your-writes consistency on standbys via WAIT FOR LSN with optional timeout that errors if the replica doesn't catch up. Willison links the pattern to MediaWiki's long-standing replication-lag handling.

candidates.title: Token fraud is here and it’s BAD (YouTube)
candidates.author: Simon Willison (on Claire Vo's video)
candidates.what_changed: Claire Vo (ChatPRD) reports organised abuse of AI product free trials to resell tokens or run businesses on her agent; she is ending free trials.
candidates.mechanism: Loops of free trials and promo codes, then tunnelling into the product's agent (e.g. a Roblox/Fortnite map studio building maps through ChatPRD). Abusers ran 'pelican riding a bicycle' SVG prompts, likely to fingerprint the underlying model family.
candidates.evidence_quality: Single operator's first-hand account via video and X post; no quantified losses in Willison's summary.
candidates.relevance: MEDIUM-HIGH for teams shipping AI products with free tiers: watch for model-fingerprinting probe prompts and trial-cycling; per-account token budgets and abuse detection are now cost controls.
candidates.overlap_with_prior: Touches cost topics but new angle (abuse/fraud).
candidates.summary: ChatPRD has been live since the GPT-4 era. Claire Vo describes a flood of token fraud: groups cycling free trials and promo codes to get free AI usage, often reselling tokens or running commercial operations on top of the ChatPRD agent ('I am funding an international Roblox and Fortnite map studio'). A common prompt was SVGs of pelicans on bicycles, which Willison suspects is used to sniff the underlying model since model families have distinctive output signatures. Vo is winding down free trials entirely; Willison agrees it looks like the right call.
